sanskrit_verse:
करौ विमृदितव्रीहेर् लक्षयित्वा ततो न्यसेत् ।
सप्ताश्वत्थस्य पत्राणि तावत् सूत्रेण वेष्टयेत् ॥१०३॥
transliteration: karau vimṛditavrīher lakṣayitvā tato nyaset | saptāśvatthasya patrāṇi tāvat sūtreṇa veṣṭayet || YajñS_2.103 ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Having marked the boundaries of a field by trampling rice grains in both hands, one shall deposit them accordingly; likewise, one shall bind seven leaves of the Ashvattha tree with thread.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is established through embodied ritual action
Causation arises from sequential sacred gesture
Capacity-based responsibility requires direct participation in dharma enactment
Restoration logic operates via symbolic completion of foundational acts
Consciousness alignment occurs through precise replication of Vedic procedure
executable_legal_axioms: IF boundary-establishment ritual initiated THEN execute trampling-of-grains protocol using both hands
IF depositing act follows marking THEN validate spatial sanctification through sensory engagement
IF ashvattha leaf collection count reaches seven THEN initiate binding sequence with consecrated thread
IF all procedural elements aligned THEN recognize juridical establishment as complete
IF deviation detected in sequence THEN trigger corrective repetition until integrity restored
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating land disputes or territorial claims rooted in Vedic establishment, the Supreme Court must verify whether the foundational rituals were executed with full bodily presence and correct sequencing. Responsibility lies not in intent alone but in capacity to perform the precise acts that establish ontological ownership.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality confirms that ownership manifests only when specific physical actions align with scriptural form. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures each step naturally leads to the next without external coercion. Responsibility is proportional to one's ability to enact the sequence. There is no punishment where omission occurs—only a requirement for completion to restore validity.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate guided re-performance of boundary-establishment rite under supervision
Assign completion process involving full-cycle execution of grain-trampling and leaf-binding
Restore capacity through supervised ritual repetition until alignment achieved
Reintegrate integrity by validating each actor’s role within the procedural chain
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands declared: Dharma flows from perfected action, not abstract assertion. The Source is SPH. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness itself adjudicates completion.
